items.message: Error message reflects back the raw env-var value `ceiling` into a user-facing report without sanitisation. If `IN_LOCKSTEP_MAX_BUDGET_USD` contains control characters or very long attacker-controlled content, it is embedded verbatim into `report.add(...)` and then emitted to stdout or JSON output. The list of required policy names (`IN_LOCKSTEP_REQUIRED_POLICIES`) is split on commas and each stripped name is compared against present layers, then the present-layer set is embedded in the error message: `', '.join(sorted(present))`. The `present` set is derived from `lockstep.policy.layers`, which comes from the repository module loaded via `_load_configured`. The broad `except Exception: return None` in `_load_configured` silently swallows all load errors, including import errors that may themselves be caused by the repository module attempting side-effects at import time. This is noted in the docstring as intentional (load failures are loud elsewhere).
